meetings.title: Cape Town One-Day Tour
meetings.global_goals: Agree on a single one-day itinerary in Cape Town that keeps a reasonable pace, fits within a modest budget, and accounts for transit and meal timing.

participants.name: Naledi Maseko
participants.background: A local architecture graduate student who has one free day to show visiting friends around the city.
participants.preferences: Prefers a structured route with short transit hops, enjoys historical districts and scenic viewpoints, dislikes rushing, wants lunch at a reliable mid-range cafe, and needs the day to end before evening commitments.
participants.personal_goals: Visit the Company's Garden, spend time at the Iziko South African Museum, and include a stop at Signal Hill for sunset views.

participants.name: Owen Hart
participants.background: An outdoor photographer traveling with a small camera kit and hoping to capture iconic city-and-coast scenes in one day.
participants.preferences: Likes early starts, panoramic views, coastal walks, and colorful neighborhoods; dislikes long indoor museum sessions and overly packed schedules; prefers at least one good coffee stop and enough time for photography.
participants.personal_goals: Ride the Table Mountain Aerial Cableway, photograph Bo-Kaap streets, and fit in a walk along the Sea Point Promenade.

participants.name: Priya Desai
participants.background: A food-focused traveler who plans trips around memorable meals and markets, and is visiting Cape Town for the first time.
participants.preferences: Prioritizes local cuisine, market browsing, and relaxed meal breaks; likes neighborhoods with lively atmosphere; dislikes expensive tasting menus and too many uphill walks; wants a route that leaves room for spontaneous snack stops.
participants.personal_goals: Browse the Oranjezicht City Farm Market or a similar local market, try a Cape Malay lunch in Bo-Kaap, and end the day with a dessert or tea stop near the Waterfront.

conversation_history.name: Naledi_Maseko
conversation_history.content:
[Steps]
[Step 1/10 - ask]
Hi everyone! I'm Naledi, and I'll be helping coordinate our tour today. Before we dive into the details, I'd love to hear what each of you is most excited to see or experience in Cape Town. Owen, what are you hoping to make this day memorable with?
Ask: Owen Hart
AskA: Hi Naledi! I’m thrilled to be here. Since I’m traveling light with just a small camera kit, I’m really hoping to maximize the outdoor shots. My dream day would start with the Table Mountain Aerial Cableway for those iconic panoramic views, followed by wandering through Bo-Kaap to capture the vibrant streets. I’d love to wrap up with a coastal walk along the Sea Point Promenade. Just a small note—I’d really appreciate a good coffee stop in between to recharge before the lens gets heavy!
[Step 2/10 - ask]
That sounds like a great plan, Owen! Table Mountain and Bo-Kaap are classics. Priya, I haven't heard from you yet—what are you hoping to see or do today? I want to make sure we balance everyone's interests while keeping the pace relaxed.
Ask: Priya Desai
AskA: Hi Naledi! Thanks for asking. Honestly, for me, the food and the vibe are what make a trip. I'd really love to start with the Oranjezicht City Farm Market because I can't resist browsing those local stalls and trying fresh produce—it's exactly that kind of lively atmosphere I'm hoping for. Since Owen mentioned Bo-Kaap, that's a perfect overlap for me too because I really want to try a Cape Malay lunch there; the flavors are unique and fit our modest budget better than expensive tasting menus. We can grab a coffee on the way from the market to your preferred spot. To wrap up, I think ending near the Waterfront for a dessert or tea would be lovely. Let's keep the pace relaxed so we can actually enjoy the snacks and meals without rushing or too many steep climbs.
[Step 3/10 - conclude]
I've put together a draft that balances everyone's wishes while keeping the pace relaxed. We'd start at the Oranjezicht Market, then move to Table Mountain for the views. Lunch would be in Bo-Kaap, which fits everyone's food interests. Then we'd visit the Iziko Museum and Company's Garden. In the late afternoon, we'd head to Signal Hill for the sunset before finishing at the Waterfront. I've estimated the costs to stay under $100, with the cableway being the main expense. Does this sequence feel like it works for everyone?

[Route Proposal]
1. Oranjezicht City Farm Market (09:00, 60 min stay, $0) - Start of day 0 min: Start with local produce and vibrant atmosphere; a great place to recharge.
2. Table Mountain Aerial Cableway (10:20, 100 min stay, $35) - MyCiTi Bus 20 min: Iconic panoramic views and outdoor photography opportunities.
3. Bo-Kaap (12:25, 95 min stay, $20) - Uber/MyCiTi 25 min: Cape Malay lunch in a colorful, historic neighborhood.
4. Iziko South African Museum (14:15, 75 min stay, $20) - MyCiTi Bus 15 min: Explore Cape Town's history and culture in a detailed exhibit.
5. Company's Garden (15:35, 30 min stay, $0) - Walk 5 min: Relax in the historic gardens adjacent to the museum.
6. Signal Hill (16:15, 60 min stay, $0) - Walk 10 min: Short hike for sunset views over the city.
7. Victoria & Alfred Waterfront (17:30, 20 min stay, $0) - Walk 15 min: End the day with a dessert or tea along the coast.

conversation_history.name: Aino_Laaksonen
conversation_history.content:
[Steps]
[Step 1/10 - ask]
Hi Jonas! Since we're starting fresh, I'd love to know what you're most excited about. Do you have any specific spots in mind, or maybe a certain vibe (like more museums vs. waterfront)? That'll help me balance the walking route with my personal stops at the Cathedral, Market Square, and Oodi.
Ask: Jonas Mäkelä
AskA: Hi Aino, thanks for asking. Since I'm here with a camera bag and limited time before my evening train, I'm most excited about securing good natural light and scenic viewpoints. My priority is capturing photos at Suomenlinna, walking along the harbor near Kauppatori, and catching a sunset viewpoint if the schedule allows. While I respect your plans for the Cathedral and Oodi, I'd prefer we keep the route outdoors rather than inside museums, as the light and views are much better for my goals. Let's try to weave your stops in without losing those outdoor moments.
[Step 2/10 - ask]
Thanks Jonas, that's really helpful regarding the light and Suomenlinna. Before I sketch out a draft, Mira - what are your priorities? Are you leaning towards museums, food, or the waterfront? I want to make sure we balance my stops at the Cathedral and Oodi with everyone's interests, keeping the budget and walking time in mind.
Ask: Mira Patel
AskA: Hi Aino! I’m so excited to plan this. For me, the priority is definitely food and markets—I just think eating through the city makes the trip so much more memorable! My main goals are trying the salmon soup at a market café and browsing the Old Market Hall, plus a cinnamon bun break later on. Since I love casual spots over formal dining, the Market Hall fits perfectly with Jonas’s harbor plans since it’s right there at Kauppatori. Let’s try to keep museums light and focus on those relaxed food breaks instead!
[Step 3/10 - conclude]
Hi everyone! Based on what Jonas and Mira just shared, I've mapped out a sequence that hits my personal favorites while keeping everyone happy. We could start at Oodi Library at 9 AM—that's my priority, and Jonas, the modern architecture there gives a nice contrast to the light you're after. From there, a quick 15-minute walk gets us to the Cathedral area, which I need to see, and from there we can head straight to Market Square around 10:30. This spot is perfect because it satisfies Mira's desire for the salmon soup and market browsing, and Jonas, the harbor views are right there. After lunch, we'd take the ferry to Suomenlinna for that golden hour light you mentioned, returning in time for a harbor walk before heading back to Oodi for Mira's cinnamon bun break around 5 PM. This keeps transit hops short and avoids the backtracking I dislike, all while staying well under the $100 budget. Does this flow work for your schedules?

[Route Proposal]
1. Oodi Library (09:00, 60 min stay, $0): Modern architecture & quiet study space (My priority).
2. Helsinki Cathedral Area (10:45, 60 min stay, $0) - Walk 45 min: Iconic architecture & ice sculpture (My goal).
3. Market Square (12:00, 90 min stay, $20) - Walk 15 min: Old Market Hall for salmon soup & lunch (Mira's priority).
4. Suomenlinna Fortress (14:15, 120 min stay, $0) - Ferry 45 min: Scenic fortress views & golden hour light (Jonas's priority).
5. Oodi Library (Return) (17:25, 35 min stay, $5) - Ferry + Walk 70 min: Cinnamon bun break & wrap up the day.

conversation_history.name: Malik_Chen
conversation_history.content:
[Steps]
[Step 1/10 - ask]
Hi Tessa, since we're starting fresh on this route, I'd love to hear what works best for you. Do you have any strong preferences for starting location or particular areas you'd like to see? I'm thinking of beginning with The Rocks since I want to walk through that historic area early, but I want to make sure it fits with your photography needs and transit preferences.
Ask: Tessa Ward
AskA: Hi Malik! That's a thoughtful question. I think starting from Circular Quay would actually work better for me - it puts us right next to the Opera House area, which is one of my top priorities. From there, we could do a quick photo stop at Mrs Macquarie's Point, then head to a waterfront café for lunch before exploring The Rocks in the afternoon. This way we minimize backtracking and keep our transit efficient. I'm flexible on the timing though - what do you think about this flow?
[Step 2/10 - ask]
Thanks Tessa, that's a helpful starting point. Before I put together a proposal, I'd like to hear from Rina as well - do you have any particular areas or attractions you'd be interested in seeing? I'm trying to balance architectural heritage sites with modern design, and I want to make sure the route works for everyone's preferences.
Ask: Rina Patel
AskA: Hi Malik! I'm so excited to weigh in. Honestly, for me, the food scene is definitely the highlight of any Sydney trip. I'd love to grab a quick breakfast at a local cafe near Circular Quay—maybe something with a view of the Opera House to start the day right. After that, I really want to hit the Sydney Fish Market. I know it can get busy, but the energy and the casual food stalls fit my style perfectly without the long restaurant sit-downs. I'm hoping we can keep the afternoon light and save the big meal for dinner in Newtown or Darling Harbour, where there are plenty of lively, affordable options. It keeps the budget tight and hits all my personal food goals!
[Step 3/10 - conclude]
Based on what Tessa and Rina have shared, let me propose a route that incorporates everyone's priorities while including my architectural interests. Here's my suggestion:

Start at Circular Quay around 9:30 - grab that breakfast with Opera House views Rina mentioned. Then do a quick 15-minute walk to Mrs Macquarie's Point for Tessa's photo opportunity before heading to the Sydney Fish Market for a casual lunch. 

After that, we'd take a short 15-minute bus ride to the Art Gallery of NSW (my top goal) - about 45 minutes for the visit including time to observe the historic building's architecture. Then we'd walk to the Museum of Contemporary Art across the road - another 30-minute visit to see modern design contrasts with the heritage sites we've seen. 

Finally, we'd take a 20-minute walk through The Rocks in the late afternoon to complete my personal goal of experiencing that historic area, and finish with dinner options in Darling Harbour as Rina suggested.

This keeps transit efficient between locations, stays within budget with mostly free admission options, and balances indoor museum time with outdoor walking. Total estimated travel time between stops is under 15 minutes each. Does this route work for everyone's preferences?

4. Art Gallery of NSW (12:25, 45 min stay, $15) - Bus 15 min: Observe historic building architecture and exhibitions
5. Museum of Contemporary Art (13:15, 30 min stay, $15) - Walk 5 min: Modern design contrast with heritage sites
6. The Rocks (13:55, 60 min stay, $0) - Walk 10 min: Historic architecture walk
7. Darling Harbour (15:15, 60 min stay, $25) - Walk 20 min: Dinner in lively, affordable area

meetings.title: Melbourne One-Day Tour
meetings.global_goals: Agree on a single one-day itinerary in Melbourne that keeps a reasonable pace, fits within a modest budget, and accounts for transit and meal timing.

participants.name: Grace Holloway
participants.background: A museum educator visiting Melbourne for a short break; she likes structuring days around a few meaningful stops and clear transit connections.
participants.preferences: Prefers art, architecture, and well-curated indoor stops; dislikes rushed schedules and long backtracking; prioritizes walkability, ticketed attractions with timed entry, and a comfortable lunch break.
participants.personal_goals: Visit the National Gallery of Victoria and see the laneways street art around the CBD, then finish with a relaxed coffee stop in Fitzroy.

participants.name: Noah Kim
participants.background: A hobbyist photographer on a weekend trip, always looking for visually distinctive scenes and places with strong natural light.
participants.preferences: Prefers scenic waterfronts, open-air markets, and neighborhoods with colorful details; dislikes overly packed indoor schedules and expensive paid experiences; wants time for photo stops and sunset views.
participants.personal_goals: Photograph the Royal Botanic Gardens, walk along Southbank, and get to a good lookout or riverfront spot for late-afternoon city views.

participants.name: Leila Haddad
participants.background: A food-focused traveler who is in Melbourne to explore local neighborhoods and sample distinctive eats without spending too much.
participants.preferences: Likes markets, casual eateries, and neighborhoods with strong local character; dislikes formal fine dining and overly touristic restaurants; prioritizes a good brunch, a memorable snack, and efficient transit between food stops and sights.
participants.personal_goals: Eat at Queen Victoria Market, try a specialty pastry or pie in a local café, and end the day with dinner in a lively neighborhood like Carlton or Brunswick.

meetings.global_goals: Agree on a single one-day itinerary in Montreal that keeps a reasonable pace, fits within a modest budget, and accounts for transit and meal timing.

participants.name: Camille Gervais
participants.background: A museum educator who lives in Montreal and is hosting two visiting friends for a short layover. She knows the city well and wants to make the most of the daylight hours.

meetings.global_goals: Agree on a single one-day itinerary in Melbourne that keeps a reasonable pace, fits within a modest budget, and accounts for transit and meal timing.

participants.name: Charlotte Nguyen
participants.background: Charlotte is visiting Melbourne for the first time on a short work trip and has one free day before her flight home. She likes being organized and has already checked transit maps and museum hours.
participants.preferences: Prefers a well-structured plan with clear start and end times; likes local coffee, compact neighborhoods, and indoor options if the weather changes; dislikes rushed transfers and overly late dinners; wants to keep spending moderate.
participants.personal_goals: Visit the National Gallery of Victoria, have coffee in a laneway café, and spend time in the Royal Botanic Gardens.

participants.name: Samir Patel

participants.personal_goals: Shoot photos in Hosier Lane, walk around the Southbank promenade, and catch sunset views from St Kilda Pier.

participants.name: Elena Petrov
participants.background: Elena is a graduate student with a strong interest in history and food culture. She is traveling on a student budget and wants the itinerary to include at least one memorable meal without being expensive.
participants.preferences: Prefers authentic local food, heritage architecture, and places that are easy to reach by tram; dislikes expensive tasting menus and overly packed schedules; values one or two standout experiences over many short stops.
participants.personal_goals: Explore Queen Victoria Market, visit Fitzroy Gardens and Captain Cook’s Cottage, and try a casual dinner in Carlton or the CBD.

conversation_history.content:

[Step 1/10 - ask]
Hi Samir, I'm Charlotte and I'll be helping us map out the day. Since we have a tight budget and time window, I want to make sure we hit the highlights everyone enjoys. I'm leaning towards the NGV, a laneway café, and the Botanic Gardens to keep things relaxed. Samir, do you have any specific spots or activities you're really keen on seeing today?
Ask: Samir Patel
AskA: Hi Charlotte, thanks for starting us off! I love the relaxed vibe of the Botanic Gardens, but as a photographer, I really feel Hosier Lane is a must for the street art vibe before the crowds peak. I think a walk along the Southbank promenade gives us that colorful waterfront energy we want without the museum ticket cost. If we can end the day at St Kilda Pier for the sunset, we'll get those golden hour shots that make the day memorable without burning our budget on indoor stops.
[Step 2/10 - ask]
Thanks Samir, that sounds like a great mix of art and scenery! I'm trying to keep transit low since we're on a budget. Elena, do you have any specific places you'd love to see today, or any dietary preferences for lunch?
Ask: Elena Petrov
AskA: Hi Charlotte, thanks for asking! For lunch, I'd love to prioritize the Queen Victoria Market. It offers authentic local food at a student budget price, whereas a laneway cafe can get pricey. I'd also love to swap the Botanic Gardens for Fitzroy Gardens and Captain Cook's Cottage. Since I'm really interested in heritage architecture and history, those spots align more with my personal goals. Also, Fitzroy is easily reachable by tram from the market, keeping our transit costs low. I'm hoping we can end with a casual dinner in Carlton nearby. What do you think about prioritizing the Market and the Cottage over the Gardens?
[Step 3/10 - reflect]
Reflecting on the discussion, I see a strong overlap in the CBD area. Samir's Hosier Lane is just a short walk from the NGV, which aligns with my goal to visit the gallery. The Botanic Gardens are right next door, perfect for my second goal. This keeps transit low and time efficient. Elena's Queen Victoria Market is a bit further, but accessible by tram, and offers the budget-friendly lunch she prefers. St Kilda seems too far for our $100 budget if we include transit. I'm thinking of proposing a route that anchors the day in the CBD to ensure we hit my personal goals (NGV, Gardens, Laneway Café) while accommodating Samir's street art interest and Elena's market preference for lunch. I'll need to check the exact transit costs, but a compact route seems best for us.
[Step 4/10 - conclude]
Hi everyone, I've put together a route that balances my priorities with yours while keeping transit and costs in check. Here is my proposal:

09:00 - National Gallery of Victoria (I'm keen to see this, and Samir, Hosier Lane is a 5-min walk for your street art).
10:30 - Coffee in a nearby laneway (my personal goal).
12:00 - Lunch at Queen Victoria Market (Elena, this keeps lunch budget-friendly).
13:30 - Royal Botanic Gardens (I really want to visit this).
15:30 - Southbank Promenade (Samir, for the waterfront views).
17:30 - Wrap up.

This avoids the transit cost of St Kilda or Fitzroy Gardens, which might push us over budget. Elena, does this work for your lunch preference, and Samir, is the flow okay?

meetings.title: Milan One-Day Tour
meetings.global_goals: Agree on a single one-day itinerary in Milan that keeps a reasonable pace, fits within a modest budget, and accounts for transit and meal timing.

participants.name: Giulia Ferri
participants.background: Giulia is a local architecture graduate student who often hosts visiting friends and likes assembling efficient city walks around major landmarks.
participants.preferences: Prefers historic streets, cathedral viewpoints, and compact walking routes; dislikes spending too long in queues; prioritizes early starts and lunch at a sit-down café; prefers using public transit sparingly.
participants.personal_goals: Visit the Duomo rooftop terrace, stop by the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, and include a short break at a classic Milanese café near the center.

participants.name: Marco Bellini
participants.background: Marco is a freelance photographer on a short work break, eager to capture the city’s atmosphere without rushing from place to place.
participants.preferences: Likes scenic viewpoints, elegant storefronts, and photo-friendly neighborhoods; dislikes overplanned schedules and crowded indoor museums; prefers flexible time for spontaneous stops; wants at least one relaxed meal.
participants.personal_goals: Photograph the Navigli canal area, get golden-hour shots of a piazza or arcade, and spend time at a traditional trattoria for dinner.

participants.name: Sara Haddad
participants.background: Sara is a museum educator traveling with limited time and a strict budget, but she still wants a meaningful mix of culture and good food.
participants.preferences: Likes one significant museum or cultural stop, affordable lunch options, and easy transit connections; dislikes expensive tasting menus and excessive walking between far-apart sites; prioritizes clear timing and value.
participants.personal_goals: Visit the Pinacoteca di Brera or another major art collection, try an inexpensive lunch near the museum district, and end the day with gelato or a simple aperitivo.

conversation_history.name: Giulia_Ferri
conversation_history.content:
[Steps]
[Step 1/10 - ask]
Hi Marco, before we finalize the itinerary, I'd love to hear your priorities. Are there any specific neighborhoods or experiences you're looking to prioritize today?
Ask: Marco Bellini
AskA: Hi Giulia, that's a great question! As a photographer on a break, I really want to focus on the atmosphere rather than ticking off a checklist. My top priorities are definitely capturing the Navigli canal area for its light and vibe, getting those golden-hour shots at a piazza or arcade, and ending with a relaxed meal at a traditional trattoria. I prefer a flexible schedule that allows for spontaneous stops over a packed itinerary, so I hope we can find a route that fits those moments without rushing and stays within our budget. Let's make it work!
[Step 2/10 - ask]
Hi Sara, thanks for joining Marco! Marco mentioned he's keen on the Navigli area and some relaxed moments. What are your top priorities for today's tour? Are there specific sites or neighborhoods you'd love to see?
Ask: Sara Haddad
AskA: Hi Giulia, my primary focus is securing a high-value cultural anchor like the Pinacoteca di Brera, which offers the best educational return for our budget. I'm looking for an affordable lunch within walking distance of the museum to minimize transit costs and time, which contrasts with routes that require long commutes between distant sites. This structure allows us to keep the morning efficient while leaving the afternoon flexible for Marco's photography needs in Navigli. I'll also prefer to end with gelato rather than an expensive dinner to stay under the $100 limit.

meetings.title: Bergen One-Day Tour
meetings.global_goals: Agree on a single one-day itinerary in Bergen that keeps a reasonable pace, fits within a modest budget, and accounts for transit and meal timing.

participants.name: Solveig Nilsen
participants.background: A local-history graduate student spending a weekend in Bergen for research notes and a short break from coursework.
participants.preferences: Likes historic districts, waterfront views, and efficient public transit; dislikes long backtracking, expensive tourist traps, and overly packed schedules; prioritizes a calm pace with time for photos and coffee.
participants.personal_goals: Visit Bryggen, take the Fløibanen up Mount Fløyen, and stop at a small café for a Norwegian pastry and coffee.

participants.name: Elias Berg
participants.background: A freelance photographer traveling with a lightweight camera kit and hoping to capture distinctive city views in one day.
participants.preferences: Likes panoramic viewpoints, soft natural light, and walkable neighborhoods; dislikes rushed transit changes and indoor-only plans; prioritizes scenic stops and enough time for photography.
participants.personal_goals: Photograph the harbor from Bryggen, shoot sunset-colored city views from a hilltop lookout, and walk a route with good street scenes and harbor reflections.

participants.name: Nadia Karim
participants.background: A teacher on a short solo trip who wants a balanced day that includes local food and a few memorable cultural stops.
participants.preferences: Likes local markets, cozy lunch spots, and combining culture with food; dislikes excessive walking without breaks, pricey tasting menus, and overly specialized museum days; prioritizes a satisfying lunch and a relaxed afternoon.
participants.personal_goals: Try a seafood lunch at the fish market, browse a local market or craft area, and end the day with a relaxed harbor-side dinner.

conversation_history.name: Solveig_Nilsen
conversation_history.content:
[Steps]
[Step 1/10 - ask]
Hi everyone! I'm Solveig, and I'm here to help us plan a great day in Bergen. Since we have limited time (9am to 6pm) and a budget of $100, I want to make sure we hit the highlights without rushing. Elias, what are you most excited to see? Are there specific historic sites or views you'd like to prioritize?
Ask: Elias Berg
AskA: Thanks, Solveig. My priority is Bryggen, a historic site, for the harbor reflections and a hilltop lookout for the sunset views. I propose a walkable route to minimize transit time and costs, which fits our budget better and allows more time for photography than rushing between locations.
[Step 2/10 - ask]
Thanks for sharing that, Elias! Bryggen and a hilltop view are definitely must-see spots. I'm curious, Nadia—what are you most looking forward to? Are there any particular museums, viewpoints, or maybe a specific type of meal you'd like to include in the day?
Ask: Nadia Karim
AskA: Oh, I'm so excited! For me, honestly, the real highlight is the food and the local vibe. I really want to try that fresh seafood lunch at the fish market—it's a personal goal for this trip to support local vendors. I'd also love to browse the craft areas nearby, maybe picking up a small souvenir. And I think ending with a relaxed harbor-side dinner is so much better than rushing. I want to make sure we balance culture with a satisfying meal on a budget!
[Step 3/10 - conclude]
Hi everyone, I've been thinking about how to weave our interests together while keeping the pace calm. Since we all want Bryggen and Fløyen offers the best hilltop views (plus it's a key part of my personal research goals), I'd like to propose this route: Start with Bryggen at 09:00 for historic exploration and waterfront photos. Around 12:00, head to the Fish Market for a fresh seafood lunch—perfect for Nadia. Then, take the Fløibanen up Fløyen at 13:30 for the views Elias mentioned. We can grab coffee and a Norwegian pastry at a small café on the hill around 15:00, which I think will be a lovely, budget-friendly break. Finally, walk back through Vågen for some craft browsing before wrapping up by 17:00. This keeps transit efficient and ensures we hit all our specific goals without rushing. What do you think?

1. Bryggen (09:00, 90 min stay, $0) - Start 0 min: Historic Hanseatic wharf with waterfront photos and historic exploration

4. Small Café on Fløyen (15:15, 60 min stay, $10) - Walk 5 min: Norwegian pastry and coffee break
5. Vågen Harbor Area (16:35, 60 min stay, $0) - Walk 20 min: Craft browsing and harbor-side views
